findings.title: Lack of Strict Path Normalization
findings.description: The code uses `decodeURI` on pathnames before passing them to the filesystem layer via `send`. While standard, double-decoding or encoding-based attacks could potentially bypass filter checks that look for specific characters.
steps_to_exploit: The server decodes it and performs check on the decoded result, but if it re-encodes, it might cause inconsistencies.
Bypass logic that relies on literal path strings.

findings.title: Improper Input Sanitization in `getPathnameForSend`
findings.description: Decoding URI components in `getPathnameForSend` after path prefix matching might allow traversal if the decoding results in '..' sequences.
steps_to_exploit: The server decodes the sequence, bypassing filters, and accesses the file.
findings.impact: Bypassing path restrictions to read unauthorized files.

findings.title: Unsafe consumption of `req.raw.url`
findings.description: The plugin frequently accesses `req.raw.url` without consistent normalization before path resolution. This can lead to bypasses where different web servers or proxies interpret encoded URLs differently than the application.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a URL with unusual encoding or path separators (e.g., `//`),
Verify if the `pumpSendToReply` logic processes it differently than the upstream proxy
findings.impact: Security control bypass; access to unintended resources.
